newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan rises ahead of Kemano announcement.
newsitem.headline: Alcan rises ahead of Kemano announcement.

text.p: Shares of Alcan Aluminium Ltd rose sharply on Tuesday ahead of a news conference at which Alcan and the British Columbia government were expected to annouce a settlement of the lawsuit on the company's canceled Kemano hydroelectric project.

Alcan Chief Executive Jaques Bougie and British Columbia Premier Glen Clark were to announce at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT in Vancouver an "important development" in negotiations on the Kemano Completion Project.
Alcan and British Columbia government officials declined to elaborate, but on Monday an official with the premier's office told Reuters that the announcement would be "good news."

In trading shortly after the open on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Tuesday, Alcan shares rose 2.10 to 55.70. The Toronto Stock Exchange was closed on Monday for a civic holiday. By mid-morning on Tuesday, Alcan was up 1.40 to 55.
In mid-morning trading on Tuesday on the Montreal Exchange, which was open on Monday, Alcan was up 0.70 to 55.
In the dispute, Alcan was seeking compensation for its Kemano hydroelectric project, which the British Columbia government canceled in 1995 after it was half-completed.
Alcan wrote down its US$420 million investment in the canceled project in the third quarter of 1995, and sued the provincial government for compensation.
Discussions between the two had focused on the province's selling power to Alcan at the same cost the Kemano plant would have provided.
The province introduced legislation last Wednesday paving the way for such an agreement. Alcan welcomed the legislation, saying it moved the two sides closer to an agreement.
The additional hydroelectric power would be needed if Alcan decided to proceed with a C$1 billion expansion of its aluminum smelter in Kitimat, British Columbia.
